items.name: Social Security Disability (SSDI) & Medicare
items.forWhat: Monthly disability income. ALS is a Compassionate Allowance, so claims are fast-tracked. The 5-month SSDI waiting period is waived for ALS, and Medicare starts when SSDI begins.
items.window: Apply as soon as you are diagnosed and unable to work.
eligibility: ALS diagnosis
Enough work credits (SSI is an option for those without)
youllNeed: Medical records confirming the ALS diagnosis
Work history and earnings
Birth certificate, SSN, bank info for direct deposit
Doctor and clinic contact details
items.howToApply: Apply online at ssa.gov/disability or call 1-800-772-1213. Say 'ALS' so the claim is flagged as a Compassionate Allowance.
items.verifyNote: SSA disability landing page live (modified 2025-12-18). Describes SSDI generally; ALS/Compassionate Allowance and phone not on this page but no contradiction.

items.name: VA Disability Compensation for ALS
items.forWhat: Tax-free monthly compensation, health care, auto and housing grants, and caregiver support. ALS is presumptively service connected and typically rated at 100%.
items.window: Apply any time.
eligibility: Veteran with 90+ days of continuous active service
ALS diagnosis
youllNeed: DD-214 (discharge papers)
ALS diagnosis records
VA Form 21-526EZ
items.howToApply: File on VA.gov or work with an accredited Veterans Service Officer (free).
items.verifyNote: Unread 2026-10-24: Fetch failed twice (client_error from va.gov). Could not read page; record unverified. Likely bot-blocking rather than a dead page.

items.window: Always available.
eligibility: Anyone (each program sets its own rules)
youllNeed: Medication names
Insurance details
items.howToApply: Search by drug or diagnosis on NeedyMeds.
items.verifyNote: Unread 2026-10-24: Page returned only metadata (JS-rendered), no readable content on homepage or /pap. Could not verify; no evidence of discontinuation.

items.name: Communication Device & Voice Banking Help

Current speech and access abilities

items.verifyNote: Live. Lists voice banking and Tech Evaluation & Access for pALS; services described as free; NY State initiative noted. No pause notice.

items.name: Technology, Equipment & Care Services

Team Gleason Adventures (trips within the US for the person with ALS and chosen companions) is listed separately under grants.

items.verifyNote: Live (modified 2026-02-06). Technology & Equipment, Care Services and Adventure still listed; read FAQs then apply via form. No deadlines or pause notice.

items.howToApply: Visit Hope Loves Company for current programs.
items.verifyNote: Live. Lists Camp HLC, Beyond the Bunk, Parent Meet Ups, Young Adult Peer Support Circle, HLC From Anywhere. No scholarship mention or dates on homepage.

items.name: Medicare (starts with SSDI for ALS)
items.forWhat: For people with ALS, Medicare coverage begins the same month SSDI benefits start, with no 24-month wait. It covers clinic visits, many tests, durable medical equipment like wheelchairs and BiPAP, and hospice.
items.window: Automatic once SSDI is approved.
eligibility: Approved for SSDI with an ALS diagnosis
youllNeed: SSDI approval
Choose Part D drug coverage and consider a Medigap or Advantage plan
items.howToApply: Enrollment follows SSDI. Ask your clinic social worker or the ALS Association Insurance & Benefits Resource Line for plan help.
items.verifyNote: Medicare.gov live; Open Enrollment banner through Dec 7 for 2027 plans. No ALS-specific text on homepage; no contradiction.

items.forWhat: Free care services for Georgians living with ALS: the Ricky P. Insurance information
Income information for the free-drug program

items.name: Paul B. Williams ALS Transportation Program
items.forWhat: Arranges and pays for door-to-door non-emergency rides (wheelchair, stretcher, or ambulatory) to ALS clinic and doctor appointments or social outings, and short accessible-van rentals through partner companies, for Georgians living with ALS. Also offers financial help toward adapting your own van or car (pre-approval required) and a $1,000 van voucher toward buying an accessible van (written request; chosen on need and impact).
items.amount: Free rides and van rentals; $1,000 van voucher and adaptation help by need
items.window: Apply any time; submit each request at least two weeks before the appointment or rental. One application per trip or rental.
eligibility: Person with ALS living in Georgia
A caregiver or companion must ride along and stay with the person on every non-emergency transport
Each trip needs pre-approval and an authorization code from the program coordinator; cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee
Van voucher and adaptation grants are awarded on need and impact
youllNeed: Transportation Program Application (online or PDF): request type, appointment date and time, pick-up and drop-off addresses, mobility equipment used
Name and phone of the adult accompanying you; signatures from both of you
For van adaptation or voucher requests, a written statement with vehicle and cost details
items.howToApply: Complete the online Transportation Program Application at alsgeorgia.org/navigating-als/transportation-program-application/ (or download the PDF) at least two weeks ahead, or call care services at 404-636-9909 to get started.

items.name: Section 504 Home Repair Loans and Grants
items.forWhat: Federal help for low-income homeowners in eligible rural areas: 1% fixed-rate loans up to $40,000 (20-year term) to repair, improve, or modernize a home or remove health and safety hazards, and grants up to $10,000 (lifetime) for very-low-income homeowners 62 and older to remove health and safety hazards. Loans and grants can be combined up to $50,000. Not ALS-specific, but a family with ALS that meets the income and rural tests can use it for ramps, bathroom changes, and similar fixes. Not ALS-specific, but it can pay for safety and accessibility repairs when a family qualifies.
items.amount: Grants up to $10,000 lifetime (age 62+); loans up to $40,000 at 1%; combined up to $50,000
items.window: Applications accepted year-round (the federal fiscal year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30); approval time depends on funding in your area.
eligibility: Own and live in the home
Home is in an eligible rural area (check the address on the USDA eligibility site)
Household income below the county's low income limit for loans, or very-low limit for grants
Unable to get affordable credit elsewhere
Grants: age 62 or older; the grant must be repaid if the home is sold within 3 years
youllNeed: Uniform Residential Loan Application (Form RD 410-4)
Forms RD 3550-1 and RD 3550-4 and the items listed in Attachment 12-E
Optional prequalification: Forms RD 3550-35 and RD 3550-1 sent to your local office
items.howToApply: Contact your local USDA Rural Development office (found through the program page) or a USDA home loan specialist in your area; they can prequalify you and take the full application.
items.contact: Local Rural Development office (see program page)
items.verifyNote: Confirmed: loans to $40,000 at 1% for 20 yrs, grants to $10,000 lifetime for age 62+, combined $50,000, grant repaid if sold within 3 years, applications year-round via local RD office. No pause notic

items.name: Jack Norton Caregiver Respite Program
items.forWhat: Scheduled breaks for the live-in family caregiver of a person with ALS in North or South Dakota. Choose coordinated respite (The ALS Association arranges a paid aide from a partner home care agency) or self-directed respite (the Association reimburses you for a caregiver you hire, who can't be the person's spouse/partner, parent or child). The program FAQ describes weekly respite in 3-4 hour blocks, up to 18 hours a month, not for emergencies and not a replacement for regular care; respite can continue during hospice.
items.amount: Free; up to 18 hours of respite a month (per the program FAQ)
items.window: Apply any time, close to when you are ready to start; allow up to two weeks for care services staff to contact you after you apply.
eligibility: The person with ALS lives in North Dakota or South Dakota
Applicant is the primary caregiver and lives with the person with ALS
Caregivers of veterans may apply, but the FAQ asks that VA home care and respite benefits be used first
youllNeed: Online application (it also serves as a release of information), then a 30-minute phone or Zoom intake with the program manager and, for coordinated respite, an in-home nursing assessment by the agency
items.howToApply: Submit the online application linked from the program page ('APPLY for the Jack Norton Caregiver Respite Program'); questions to respitemn@als.org or 888-672-0484.
items.verifyNote: Active: ND/SD residence, live-in primary caregiver; coordinated (agency aide) or self-directed (reimbursement, not spouse/parent/child); staff contact within 2 weeks; 888-672-0484, respitemn@als.org.

Verified medical need, such as dependence on a ventilator or other electricity-dependent equipment
